audit.why: EVEN 5.5/10 with a 47.81% win rate over 343 games is a fair read on a lane Aurora wins and a game she loses. Early is hers on range alone — Breath of Light and Singularity both stop at 750 against her 900-range Q — while Cosmic Creator's Stardust permanently improves his whole kit, so side lane and teamfights trend to him. The page's chart already reflects that arc.

The spikes are keyed to real numbers and to the right mechanic each time: Astral Flight 22/20.5/19/17.5/16, Singularity flat 12s, Falling Star 120/110/100 at 1250 range, and Stardust upgrading Falling Star into The Skies Descend. spikes[2] correctly frames Aurora's first item as her last clean window because his scaling never stops.

Three decisive interactions are all present and correctly stated from Riot's text. Breath of Light only earns its bonus damage for each second it is channelled directly at the target, so breaking the line is the counterplay rather than out-trading it. Astral Flight removes Breath of Light's cooldown and channel cap while he flies, making it a damage window rather than only an escape. Singularity pulls inward toward a centre that executes below a health percentage — both missingInteractions entries (execute threshold, resistances invalidated) are already covered, in spikes[3].text and dontsFull[2].d respectively.
breakdown.cooldowns carries digits and the non-obvious point: Astral Flight 22s at rank 1 and what it does to his Q, Singularity flat 12s, Falling Star 120s at rank 1.
